verses.1: And the LORD said to Moses, “Make for me two stone tablets, just as before. And I will write on them the same words that were written on the first tablets.”
verses.2: May it be that it will be possible to go there in the morning. In the morning, you will climb up to Mount Sinai. And you will stand there, on top of the mountain.
verses.3: And no one shall come up with you. Nor shall anyone be able to go up to any of the mountains. Neither the sheep nor the cattle shall be able to cross over that mountain.
verses.4: And Moses took two stone blocks, as it was commanded by God. He carried them on his shoulder and went up to Mount Sinai, just as God had instructed him. He held those two stone blocks in his hands.
verses.5: And Jehovah came down in a cloud, and stood there with him. Then he cried out in the name of Jehovah.
verses.6: And Jehovah passed by on his face. Then Jehovah called out to Him, “Elohim of mercy and compassion! May your days be long, and may your kindness and truth be great.”
verses.7: He who seeks God’s mercy will not be burdened by sins, mistakes, or transgressions. He will be cleansed from all evil. He will not suffer the punishment that parents deserve for their children, nor for their descendants.
verses.8: And Moses hurried and measured the land, and he bowed down.
verses.9: And he said, “If I have indeed won your favor, O Lord, then please let me enter among you. For this people is stubborn and unruly. But you have forgiven our sins and given us a place among you.”
verses.10: And he said, “Look, I make a covenant with all your people. I will do wonders that have never been done on this earth or in any other country. And all the people who are under your rule will see that the works of Jehovah are done by me.”
verses.11: I will guard what I have commanded you today. I will remove from before you the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Hivvites, and the Yebusites.
verses.12: Keep this covenant, so that you may not break it when you reign over the earth. Otherwise, it will become a burden upon you.
verses.13: For their idols will be destroyed, and their places of worship will be ruined. And their sacred objects will be torn apart.
verses.14: For you shall not worship another god, for Jehovah is a jealous God. He is a God who is jealous.
verses.15: Do not break the covenant with the Lord, who rules over the earth. Do not worship other gods instead of Him. Do not offer sacrifices to those idols. And do not eat from the offerings that you have offered to those idols.
verses.16: And you took their daughters as your wives. They also married your daughters in place of their own daughters. They married your daughters in the name of their gods.
verses.17: O God of sacrifices, do not do this to me.
verses.18: On the day of Passover, you shall observe it for seven days. You shall eat matzot on that day, as it is commanded by God. It is the day of Easter; because on this day you left Egypt.
verses.19: All your treasures are mine, and all your possessions will be remembered by Peter Shor Vasha.
verses.20: And if she does not take them away, then she will be destroyed completely. But if she does take them away, then your children will be destroyed as well. Then my face will no longer be seen.
verses.21: For six days, you shall work. On the seventh day, you shall rest in peace. And during the time of harvesting, you shall also rest.
verses.22: And the Harvest Festival will be celebrated in the barley-harvesting fields. And the Festival of Unleavened Bread will be celebrated at the end of the year.
verses.23: Three times a year, all remembrance of you will be remembered by the face of the altar. May the LORD, the God of Israel, remember you.
verses.24: For nations will come from before you, and I will expand your borders. No one will eat your land, except for your wives, so that they may see the face of the LORD your God three times a year.
verses.25: Do not sacrifice on the blood of an animal that has been used for sacrifice. And do not offer sacrifices on the day of Passover in the morning.
verses.26: At the beginning, in the chambers of your land, you will bring the house of Jehovah, your God. Do not defile yourself with milk from your mother’s womb.
verses.27: And the LORD said to Moses, “I have written these words for you. By these words I have made a covenant with you and with Israel.”
verses.28: And there were forty days and forty nights during which he remained with Jehovah, without eating bread or drinking water. He wrote down on the tablets the words of the covenant: twelve words in total.
verses.29: And it happened that Moses descended from Mount Sinai. The two tablets of stone were in Moses’ hands as he descended from the mountain. But Moses did not know that a smile appeared on his face while he spoke to God.
verses.30: And Aaron and all the Israelites saw Moses. They saw that there was a light coming from his face, and they were afraid of him.
verses.31: Moses called out to them, and Aaron and all the priests rushed to him. Moses spoke to them.
verses.32: And after that, all the children of Israel came forward and proclaimed what Jehovah had commanded them on Mount Sinai.
verses.33: And Moses was able to speak with them, and he showed them his face.
verses.34: And when Moses came before Jehovah to speak with Him, he would remove his sandals before leaving. Then he would go and speak to the children of Israel about what they were to do.
verses.35: And the Israelites saw Moses’ face. It was covered with sweat, and Moses wiped the sweat off his face before he could speak to them.
